ui.name: Sacramento
ui.title_cos: Placer Title, Old Republic Title, Fidelity National Title, all in Sacramento
ui.title_call: Placer Title or Old Republic Title
ui.law: California lets you assign a purchase contract. Tell the seller in writing that you are a wholesaler and may assign the contract, and never market the house itself, only your contract. California is a non-judicial foreclosure state: the lender records a Notice of Default, then a Notice of Sale, and a trustee sells the house, so pre-foreclosure filings are at the County Recorder. Escrow and title companies close, not attorneys.
ui.groups: "NorCal REIA", "Sacramento Real Estate Investors", "Sacramento Wholesale Deals"
ui.prefc: Estate: the assessor records the last document on every parcel. Death of owner, affidavit of death and probate orders mean the house just passed to heirs, who often live elsewhere and want it gone. Deceased means the roll itself still lists an estate as owner. The county does not publish owner names online, so every card says Owner of Record; the mailing address is real and is where you write or skip trace.
ui.buyers_note: Sacramento County does not publish owner names on its parcel data, so there is no buyer list from the assessor yet. Use the Zillow sold filter on the house you have under contract, or ask Placer Title for the recent cash closings in that zip.
ui.buyers_empty: No buyer list for Sacramento yet: the county hides owner names.
ui.repairs: Repairs, Sacramento rough numbers per house: cosmetic 20-35k, kitchen+baths 40-70k, roof 15-25k, HVAC 10-18k, foundation and dry rot 10-30k, full gut 90-150k.
ui.sources: Sacramento County GIS parcel base (situs, mailing address, land use, last recorded document type and date, estate status)
